Intonation with Lists, Choice Questions, and Non-final Thought Groups

Intonation is the rise and fall of your voice. There are definite and expected intonation patterns in English.  The more you practice listening to and saying the correct intonation patterns, the better you will understand and be understood.
When naming items in a list, you use rising intonation for the first item in the list and falling intonation for the last. Falling intonation indicates the end of the list.

For example:

I follow the three Rs. I recycle ⤴, reduce ⤴, and reuse ⤵.

The rising intonation indicates to the listener that you are not finished and that there are other items in the list.

All choice questions have an 'or' in them and cannot be answered by yes or no answers, and imply a choice between one option or the other.

For example:
Did you recycle that ↗ or just throw it in the trash⤵?

A thought group refers to a coherent unit of speech that forms a whole. You normally separate a long sentence into several thought groups. Non-final thought groups represent all the thought groups that you say before the last thought group of a sentence. The final thought group is the thought group that ends a sentence. You stress non-final thought groups with a normal-rising-normal pattern.

For example:
Paper consumption continues to rise ... a typical office will use approximately 1,000 sheets of paper ... per month ... per person.

Read the following sentences, keeping in mind the different intonation patterns you use:
Energy is used to light, heat and air condition a typical workplace.
Do you recycle scrap paper or toss it aside in the trash?
We must look for ways to reduce our environmental footprint and become greener—not just at home, but at the office as well.

images.text: We must look for ways to reduce our environmental footprint and go greener—not just at home, but at the office as well. We need to make small changes at the office so we can help protect our environment. If we implement environmentally friendly practices in our office, we can make a difference.

Office equipment alone will have accounted for more than 50% of the energy used in our office! If you won't be using your computer screen, you mustn't leave it on, turn it off. Screens are the biggest consumers of energy using 10% of the total energy consumed by the computer, even when on stand-by. We must reduce our energy consumption. We will save energy and make our office more environmentally friendly, and more cost-friendly.
Paper consumption continues to rise. We needn't waste anymore. Did you know that a typical office will have used approximately 1,000 sheets of paper per month per person? We must cut back on our unnecessary paper use, we need to significantly decrease our solid waste.

One obvious way to reduce the amount of greenhouse gas emissions is to reduce the amount of electricity used, since electricity generation is a major source of greenhouse gases.
Do you leave the water running when you're washing your plate at lunch or do you turn the tap off? Water is a precious resource and demand around the world will be growing as populations increase. We need to take some precautions when using it. We must help conserve it.
We mustn't sit idle! We can make a difference by taking simple steps to be more environmentally friendly. The little actions we take will have added up to big results in the long run. Get involved and start making a real impact!
